headings.title: SMTO-SKL-0066 — SMTO can't tell whether your calendar change went through

html:
SMTO-SKL-0066 — SMTO can't tell whether your calendar change went through

GUID: 53e85f74-9b72-5ca2-8c6f-9ed2507d7b54
Slug: microsoft365-calendar-mutation-outcome-unknown
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: microsoft365

What happened

  • SMTO asked Microsoft to change your calendar, but the answer was lost. The meeting may already have been created, changed or cancelled, and invitations or replies may already have gone out.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open your Outlook calendar, or ask SMTO to show your meetings for that day, without asking for any change yet. This shows whether the meeting was created, changed, cancelled or answered before the answer was lost.
  2. If the change is there, you're done. If a new meeting now appears twice, delete the extra copy in Outlook. Repeating a change that already happened can create duplicate meetings or send attendees extra invitations.
  3. Only if the change is clearly missing, ask SMTO to make it once more. SMTO never repeats calendar changes on its own because it can't be sure the first one failed.

What success looks like

  • Your Outlook calendar shows the meeting exactly once, in the state you wanted.

If it still fails

  • Check whether the earlier action already happened in Outlook before anything else. Then select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't keep asking SMTO to repeat the change until you've checked the calendar.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Microsoft 365 calendar create, update, delete, cancel or response request lost its result, and readback could not confirm whether the intended event change was applied.

What this means

  • Calendar mutation response is uncertain and any supported transaction/readback reconciliation cannot prove the intended event result. Microsoft may already have applied the mutation. A lost or unverifiable result is not proof of nonexecution; inspect exact resource and correlation evidence before another write.

Why this can happen

  • Calendar mutation response is uncertain and any supported transaction/readback reconciliation cannot prove the intended event result.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the exact calendar/event and retained transaction or request evidence.

How to fix it

  • Read the exact calendar event (or calendar_events for the window) under the same account and, for creates, look for the event matching the transaction_id in the error details. Reconcile the actual meeting state, including attendee notifications, before issuing any further calendar mutation; never replay the original request blindly.
  • Inspect the exact calendar event and transaction/request evidence; repeat no meeting mutation until its actual outcome is reconciled.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect provider state and exact account authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • The actual meeting state is reconciled before another mutation.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • Microsoft may already have applied the mutation. A lost or unverifiable result is not proof of nonexecution; inspect exact resource and correlation evidence before another write.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
